full_judgment: 11. We like to observe, here, that the Court of appeal below has committed an error of law on the question of onus, in rendering independent advice to a purdahnasheen lady. We have noted that the lady shall get independent advice before entering into the transaction on the true nature and on the consequence of such transaction, and that upon understanding the true character of the transaction shall execute the deed voluntarily with full knowledge of the transaction. The lower appellate Court erroneously, held that it could be presumed from the fact, that Akmal was near relation, and he must have given some advice. The onus is not a matter of presumption, but of evidence and must be given by the party, who is the beneficiary of the transaction by the purdahnasheen lady. However, the quantum of evidence required, will depend upon the fact and circumstance of each case. The evidence is lacking in this case. The learned Single Judge, is right in observing, that the first appellate Court, did commit this error of law.
